title: Moments of Random Permanents and Hafnians: A Replica Approach
authors: Paolo Facchi, Angelo Mariano, Giorgio Parisi, Saverio Pascazio, Antonello Scardicchio
abstract: Using contour-integral representations of the permanent and of the Hafnian, we turn the computation of their moments for random matrices into a replica calculation, analogous to that of the moments of the partition function of a mean-field spin glass. For the $2k$-th moment of $N\times N$ matrices with independent entries, the dominant saddle point is replica symmetric for $k>2$, and we obtain in closed form the exponential growth rate, the prefactor and the first $1/N$ correction, in agreement with exact enumerations. The growth rate depends only on whether the entries are real or complex; higher cumulants affect only the prefactor and the $1/N$ term. At $k=2$ the replica-symmetric solution becomes unstable, separating a power-law bulk of the distribution from a large-deviation tail, which we compute. The results apply to boson sampling with single photons and with squeezed light.
summary: This theoretical paper calculates the moments of random permanents and Hafnians using a replica approach, mirroring techniques from spin glass theory. The results provide exact asymptotic expansions for these moments, which are crucial for understanding the probability distributions in quantum photonic experiments like boson sampling. It extends random matrix theory into non-determinantal structures.
main_problem: The paper computes the moments of random permanents and Hafnians for random matrices, extending the study of random matrix theory beyond determinants.
main_result: The authors derive the exponential growth rate, prefactor, and $1/N$ correction for these moments in closed form, providing results applicable to bosonic sampling.
method: The calculation employs a replica approach, utilizing contour integrals and saddle-point analysis analogous to mean-field spin glass calculations.
model_or_system: The model involves $N 	imes N$ random matrices with i.i.d. entries (real or complex). The results have direct physical applications to boson sampling (related to permanents) and squeezed-light boson sampling (related to Hafnians).

important_parameters: Matrix size $N$, moment order $k$, and the nature of the matrix entries (real vs. complex).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the replica-symmetric saddle point approximation for $k>2$, and the calculation of $1/N$ corrections involves complex diagrammatic expansions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of a boson sampling experiment and diagrammatic representations of the $1/N$ corrections, including Dumbbell and Theta diagrams.
paper_structure: The paper develops from general integral representations of permanents/Hafnians to the replica formalism, solving the Gaussian case via saddle-point approximation to find the rate function, and finally calculating the $1/N$ corrections using diagrammatic expansions around the RS saddle point.
why_interesting: The connection between computing moments of permanents/Hafnians and the replica method used for spin glasses provides powerful, transferable mathematical tools for analyzing complex quantum optical processes like boson sampling.
